scope: Three selected primary-source targets published before 2006; original research intake, not an exhaustive census of all old papers.
review_status: The new semilinear proof passed independent internal root-agent review against the exact primary-source hypotheses. External peer review and publication priority remain unverified.

entries.title: RWPRI and (2T)1 flag-transitive linear spaces
entries.source_item: Section 5.1.2, printed page 39, question after Proposition 5.5; retained in Theorem 6.1(1), footnote 11
entries.statement: Every flag-transitive RWPRI linear space of spread type whose designated affine action lies in AGammaL(1,p^d) is Desarguesian. The one-dimensional affine hypothesis from the surrounding section is essential.
entries.precise_reduction: For a spread S of l-dimensional Fp-subspaces of F_(p^d), suppose H<=GammaL1 acts transitively and primitively on S, and H_U acts irreducibly on U for every U in S. Then S is the set of one-dimensional F_(p^l)-subspaces.
entries.reading_depth: Definitions 2.2, Proposition 5.2, Sections 5.1-5.3, and Theorem 6.1 read; not merely a keyword search.
entries.external_status: No primary later resolution of the narrowly stated RWPRI question found in targeted searches through 2026-10-09; novelty not established.
entries.project_status: Complete proposed uniform uniqueness proof with two internal independent reviews of the descent step; exact existence converse via AGL1(F) also independently checked. External priority and peer review unverified.
entries.proof_location: phase4_old_problem_audit.md, Section 1, Theorem A and Lemmas A1-A3
entries.structural_bridge: Primitive metacyclic action -> prime spread degree -> prime-power field degrees -> cyclic semilinear descent -> scalar-field lines.
entries.new_work: Lemma A3 proves irreducible scalar-by-cyclic-u actions of u-power dimension collapse to dimension one over their scalar field when p is not 1 modulo u; its application settles the mathematical uniqueness statement under the explicit source hypotheses.
retained_inputs: Source Proposition 5.2 supplies the translation/spread reduction of its one-dimensional case.
Affine local primitivity is equivalent to irreducibility of the zero stabilizer.
entries.finite_check_scope: All subspaces containing 1 for (ambient degree,line dimension)=(4,2),(8,4),(6,2) over F2, modulo scalar/Frobenius equivalence. Only subfield orbits have irreducible stabilizer in the prime-degree cases; degree six supplies a boundary control.

later_primary_evidence.finding: Constructs non-Desarguesian one-dimensional flag-transitive spread spaces without the two local primitivity assumptions. Introduction and Theorem 1/proof read in author manuscript.
Further flag-transitive families; does not by its stated hypotheses answer the RWPRI uniqueness question.

Cyclic 2-spreads in V(6,q), characteristic greater than 3. Their spread size q^4+q^2+1 is composite, excluding local primitivity for a one-dimensional action by Lemma A1. Introduction and Sections 2.1-2.4 read.
Broader orbit-polynomial classification remains under study; no claim about the narrower 2003 question.

later_primary_evidence.work: Guan-Zhou (2016), Extremely primitive groups and linear spaces
later_primary_evidence.finding: Introduction, definition, main theorems and Theorem 1.1 proof checked. Local primitivity means only pencils; the main hypothesis is extreme point primitivity. Its AG(m,3) exception does not settle the general two-sided RWPRI spread-space question.

limitations: Not a classification of all one-dimensional flag-transitive spaces.
Not a resolution of nonspread cases beyond existing source results.
No external peer review or publication-priority certification.
entries.new_consequence: For 0<l<d with l dividing d, such a one-dimensional flag-transitive RWPRI spread space exists exactly when (p^d-1)/(p^l-1) is prime. It is uniquely AG(d/l,p^l), and the group T_F semidirect F* realizes the required action.
entries.converse_scope: Classifies spaces and existence parameters in source Theorem 6.1(1); does not enumerate every possible acting subgroup.

entries.title: A generalization of a construction due to Van Nypelseer
entries.source_item: Construction 3 and Conjecture 1, Section 4.6, printed page 569
entries.statement: For every prime power q>2, the rank-three geometry built from Hermitian-unital points Q, blocks L and flags (p,M), with incidences Q not in L, Q in M minus p, and L intersect M={p}, is firm, residually connected and flag-transitive.
entries.reading_depth: Construction and conjecture were previously read in primary full text; existing full project proof re-read for this intake.
entries.external_status: No external primary resolution found in renewed exact-title and unital-specific searches; publication priority remains unverified.
entries.project_status: Earlier complete project proof with internal independent review and exact q=2,3,4,5 checks. Not counted as a newly solved target in phase four.
entries.structural_bridge: The block residue is an SU2(q) torsor on a nonzero Hermitian norm shell; root-group moves preserve connected components and generate the torsor action.
entries.new_work: This intake clarifies status and structural scope; the proof itself was completed in an earlier phase.
limitations: No new claim of external priority.
The explicit Hermitian identification remains family-specific input.

entries.title: An algorithmic analysis of the intersection property
entries.statement: In every residue, for every type i, element x and flag F, the intersection of their i-shadows is empty or the i-shadow of a flag incident to x and F. In a flag-transitive coset geometry this condition can be tested using one incident pair and orbit representatives under its stabilizer, with singleton and nested-shadow pruning.
entries.reading_depth: Sections 2-3 and Figure 1 proof/pruning observations read; sporadic tables in Sections 4-5 not recomputed.
entries.external_status: Established algorithm in the source, not an open conjecture.
entries.project_status: Exact matrix formulation derived; does not rederive all numerical table entries.
entries.structural_bridge: Incidence columns multiply entrywise to shadow vectors; admissible shadow realizations and their equality tests are equivariant under basis permutations.
entries.new_work: Integration into the basis-aware torsor calculus with an explicit distinction from the distinguished-generator subgroup intersection property.
retained_inputs: Actual admissible flag sets and residue incidence matrices.
Finite-group geometry data for numerical sporadic tables.
limitations: Geometric shadow IP is not interchangeable with C-group subgroup IP.
